body.cap: Cho Hojin, CEO of GenGenAI, introduces the company's GenGenStudio platform to AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist during CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: GenGenAI (CEO Cho Hojin) participated in CES Unveiled on January 5 (local time), a pre-event to CES 2025, showcasing its innovative dataset generation platform, GenGenStudio. The company, founded to solve challenges related to high costs, time, and data imbalances in AI training, is committed to delivering high-quality datasets to fuel advancements in autonomous driving and other cutting-edge industries.

With a vision to contribute significantly to fully autonomous AI systems, GenGenAI develops high-quality datasets capable of addressing variables such as seasons, weather, and time of day. These datasets enhance autonomous driving technologies and extend the company’s influence to the defense and security sectors.

At CES Unveiled, GenGenAI introduced GenGenStudio, a platform leveraging domain-specific generative AI technology to produce synthetic datasets, including high-quality images and videos tailored for various industries. This platform aims to shorten development timelines for organizations adopting AI while addressing privacy concerns, data shortages, and bias. The company’s ability to offer such solutions at competitive prices further broadens the accessibility of AI technologies.

GenGenAI holds over twenty patents that support the reliability of GenGenStudio’s synthetic datasets. The platform has already demonstrated its impact on mobility and autonomous driving AI development, earning recognition for its contributions. These accomplishments culminated in the platform receiving an Honoree award at the CES 2025 Innovation Award in the AI category.

body.cap: Cho Hojin, CEO of GenGenAI, introduced GenGenStudio to international media representatives during CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: GenGenAI is actively expanding its solutions to advanced industries, including defense and security, collaborating with key players to unlock its full potential. The company stated that GenGenStudio empowers organizations to accelerate and enhance AI development across diverse sectors, allowing more users to benefit from AI-driven solutions. It also addresses regulatory requirements and optimizes costs, which has earned the platform widespread recognition and adoption.

A GenGenAI representative highlighted the significance of the company’s participation in CES 2025 and Unveiled, noting, “We aim to showcase the possibilities of our technology to global automakers, vendors, and defense contractors, creating new business opportunities. Following acquiring international clients and partners, we plan to establish overseas subsidiaries in markets such as the US and Europe to accelerate our global expansion further.”

This year’s CES and Unveiled events marked a pivotal step in GenGenAI’s mission to revolutionize AI training and dataset generation, positioning itself as a key player in the rapidly evolving landscape of AI innovation.

GenGenAI participated in CES 2025 as part of the Seoul Pavilion in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion, expanded by over 50% from the previous year to 1,040 square meters, featured 104 startups. It represents a collaboration between three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Geumcheon, and Gwanak), five startup support organizations (SBA, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight universities (Konkuk, Kyung Hee, Kookmin, Dongguk, Sogang, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei, and Chung-Ang).
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
